Yes: several papers describe improving AI with self-generated feedback instead of human labels, including for following complex rules. RuleEvolve directly targets rules for coding agents by mutating candidate rules and using a judge module to evaluate and keep the best ones, outperforming manual rule engineering and prompt optimization baselines [10]. More broadly, self-improvement frameworks let models generate data, evaluate outputs, and iteratively refine capabilities with minimal or no external supervision [4].

If you mean self-feedback during reasoning or agent behavior, there are a few variants. TRT uses self-generated verification signals at test time to improve answers without external feedback [1]. CoNL uses multi-agent critique and meta-evaluation, rewarding critiques that help improve solutions, so generation and judging improve together without external judges or ground truth [8]. NRT trains reasoning models from standard question-answer pairs by having the model generate its own reasoning traces, avoiding expert-written demonstrations and external verifiers [5].
